moving-around.label: Moving Around with cd
moving-around.summary: Move between folders with cd, cd .., and simple relative paths.

sketch1.title: Use `cd ..` to go up one folder

sc-cd-purpose.title: What `cd` does
sc-cd-purpose.hint: Confirm the starting location with `pwd`, then follow the folder names in order.

help.concept: `cd` changes the current directory; `..` means one parent level and a relative path begins from the current directory.
help.hint_1: Confirm the starting location with `pwd`, then follow the folder names in order.
help.hint_2: Run `pwd` or `ls` after moving so the destination is proven rather than assumed. The current task asks: What does `cd` do?

mc-check-after-cd.hint: Think about confirming both the destination path and what is present there.

help.concept: `pwd` confirms the current path. `ls` can help confirm that the expected destination contents are present.
help.hint_1: One command reports the path itself.

cd-into-folder.title: Move Into a Folder
cd-into-folder.bodyMarkdown: `cd` changes the terminal's current working directory. A folder name can be used when that folder is inside the current location.

cd-up-one-level.title: Move to the Parent Folder
cd-up-one-level.bodyMarkdown: `cd ..` moves one directory level upward to the current folder's parent.

relative-paths.title: Navigate With Relative Paths
relative-paths.bodyMarkdown: A relative path starts from the current directory. It can cross more than one folder level without requiring the full absolute path.
